prov.heading: Provisions for Credit Losses
prov.text:
Provision for Card balance credit losses decreased for both the three and nine month periods, primarily due to reserve releases in the current periods versus reserve builds in the prior periods, partially offset by higher net write-offs. The reserve release in the current three month period was primarily driven by enhancements to the models that estimate expected credit losses resulting from our periodic review process, partially offset by a sequential increase in Card balances. The reserve release in the current nine month period was primarily driven by lower delinquencies and the previously-mentioned enhancements to the models that estimate expected credit losses, partially offset by a sequential increase in Card balances. The reserve builds in the prior periods were primarily driven by sequential increases in Card balances, partially offset by the release of a reserve upon the reclassification of a small business cobrand portfolio to Card balances HFS. The reserve build in the prior nine month period also reflected the macroeconomic outlook.

Provision for other credit losses increased for the three month period, primarily due to a higher reserve build for Other loans and higher net write-offs. Provision for other credit losses decreased in the nine month period, primarily due to a lower reserve build, partially offset by higher net write-offs.

nonint.text: Operating expenses decreased, reflecting the previously-mentioned gain from the sale of our equity interest in GBTG, partially offset by increases in legal reserves and restructuring costs. Excluding the impact of these discrete items, operating expense grew modestly. We have invested significantly in risk and controls over the last several years and will continue to make the investments necessary to strengthen our risk management and compliance programs so that they meet our expectations and those of our regulators.

Refer to Note 16 and Note 21 to the “Consolidated Financial Statements” for further details on preferred shares and earnings per common share (EPS), respectively.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Our cash flows from operating activities primarily include net income adjusted for (i) non-cash items included in net income, such as provisions for credit losses, depreciation and amortization, stock-based compensation, deferred taxes and other non-cash items and (ii) changes in the balances of operating assets and liabilities, which can vary significantly in the normal course of business due to the amount and timing of payments.

In 2024, the net cash provided by operating activities was driven by cash generated from net income for the period, partially offset by lower net operating liabilities, primarily driven by lower book overdrafts due to timing differences arising in the ordinary course of business.

In 2023, the net cash provided by operating activities was primarily driven by cash generated from net income for the period and higher net operating liabilities, primarily driven by higher book overdrafts due to timing differences arising in the ordinary course of business and higher accounts payable to merchants.

opex.text: Salaries and employee benefits and other expenses increased, primarily driven by the gain in the prior year recognized on the sale of Accertify included in the Other, net component of operating expenses, partially offset by a decrease in allocated service costs.

costs.text: Salaries and employee benefits and other expenses increased, primarily driven by the gain in the prior year recognized on the sale of Accertify included in the Other, net component of operating expenses, partially offset by a decrease in allocated service costs.

nonop.heading: TOTAL REVENUES NET OF INTEREST EXPENSE
nonop.text:
Discount revenue increased, primarily driven by an increase in billed business of 8 percent, partially offset by lower average merchant discount rates due to shifts in geographic and merchant spend mix. See Tables 5 and 6 for more details on billed business performance.

Net card fees increased, primarily driven by growth in our premium card portfolios. See Table 5 for more details on proprietary new card acquisitions, proprietary cards-in-force and average fee per card.

Service fees and other revenue increased, primarily driven by higher foreign exchange-related revenues associated with Card Member cross-currency spending, a gain related to an equity transaction by GBTG, an equity method investee, resulting from its acquisition of CWT Holdings, LLC, and increases in network partnership revenue and loyalty coalition-related fees.

Interest income increased, primarily driven by growth in revolving loan balances, partially offset by lower interest rates.

Interest expense was relatively flat, primarily reflecting lower interest rates paid on customer deposits, offset by growth in customer deposits and long-term debt.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Equity securities
lines.why: Shares held for their return: financial.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: During 2025, approximately 22 percent of our total revenues net of interest expense were generated from activities outside the United States.

The ultimate impact of any such rulemaking will depend on a number of factors, including the content of the final rulemaking, future minimum regulatory requirements and management decisions regarding our product constructs, capital distributions and target capital levels, and such rulemaking could result in significantly higher regulatory capital requirements for the Company and AENB.

We also increasingly rely on merchant acquirers, processors and payment facilitators to manage certain aspects of our merchant relationships and promote and support the acceptance and usage of our cards, but they may have business interests, strategies or goals that are inconsistent with ours.
Increasing spending on our cards also depends on our continued expansion of merchant acceptance of our cards.

We rely on third parties for certain Membership Rewards redemption options, statement credits, Card Member offers, travel- and dining-related benefits and other rewards and benefits, and we may modify or not be able to continue to offer such rewards and benefits in the future, which could diminish the value of our cards.
